affected_party: QIF evaluators, accountable reviewers, domain specialists, operators, and affected stakeholders
actual_problem: Selective escalation decisions can be recorded, but the runtime cannot yet show whether an escalation was accepted, rejected, redirected, or timed out, whether required capacity was available, or whether response-time expectations were met.
why_it_matters: An escalation recommendation without resolution evidence can create false assurance, hide unavailable authority or capability, and leave consequential uncertainty unresolved.
why_now: QIF v0.6.35 introduced governed selective escalation, while current AI oversight practice explicitly measures review latency, escalation disposition, and human review availability.
